# sq-39 — First-record ceiling for byte-limited profiling

With a byte limit, squalify reads a first record that is longer than the limit to its end, however long (sq-35, owner decision 2026-10-28: "No ceiling, document it"). Add an opt-in ceiling, `ProfileOptions.MaxFirstRecordBytes` and `--max-first-record-bytes N`: when the first record, line terminator included, is longer than N, squalify stops reading at N+1 bytes instead of reading on. **Not in this slice:** a ceiling on any record after the first; a default ceiling (off by default, so today's behavior and descriptors are unchanged); sampling from the middle or end of a file.

**Findings:**  · **Size:** S `[needs-owner]` · **Tree:** core

**2026-10-28** — OPEN QUESTIONS for the owner (not decided; the failing tests marked pending depend on them).
Q1. Outcome when the first record is longer than N. (a) SqualifyException with a clear message, nothing profiled: simplest, a consumer that wants a refusal gets one, but the CLI and library produce no descriptor. (b) An issue code (e.g. firstRecordTooLong) with scope.complete false and an empty or partial profile: the descriptor stays a result, but sq-35 decided "never an empty profile for a file with data", so this needs a partial profile of the first N+1 bytes or an explicit exception to that rule, and the cap must then be written in scope to keep descriptors self-describing and deterministic. Also decide the CLI exit code.
Q2. Does the ceiling also apply without --max-bytes? (a) Yes: it caps the first record of a whole-file profile, which then fails early on a file with no line breaks. (b) No, rejected without --max-bytes: keeps it a byte-limit companion; a whole-file run has no overshoot to bound. Note: the whole-file path never calls ScopeCut today, so (a) adds a new early read of the first record before the byte pass.
Q3. Interaction with the cuts. Proposed reading, to confirm: N counts bytes of the first record including its terminator in the charset code units (CRLF counts 2, UTF-16 terminator 2, UTF-32 4); a bare CR as byte N needs one more unit to see whether an LF follows, so reading N+1 bytes (or one unit more) is allowed for that lookahead and the record is then N+1 if it is CRLF; for UTF-16/32 stop at the first whole unit past N rather than at exactly N+1 bytes; a binary file (cut exactly at the limit, no records) is not subject. Also: does N below --max-bytes make the check run before the window sniff (the test list assumes yes)?

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

A consumer that knows its format has short header lines (a sweep-table splitter that classifies a file from its first 1 MiB) wants to refuse a huge file with no line breaks without reading all of it. Today `ScopeCut.FindLineCut` keeps reading in 4 KiB chunks until it finds a terminator or the end of the file, so a multi-gigabyte file with no line breaks is read whole. Follows sq-35, which chose "read it whole, no ceiling" as the default and said the overshoot is documented, not capped; this adds the opt-in without reopening that decision.

## Failing tests

- **Off by default:** a file whose first line is longer than `--max-bytes`, profiled without a ceiling, gives the same descriptor as before (golden, `scope.bytesRead` is the whole first line).
- **Boundary:** a first record of exactly N bytes (terminator included) is accepted; N+1 bytes triggers the ceiling.
- **Reads at most N+1 bytes:** a counting `IProfileSource` over a large file with no line break, with `MaxFirstRecordBytes` N, shows that no more than N+1 bytes were read in total, including when `MaxBytes` is larger than N+1 (the ceiling check runs before the sniff of the window, so the window read does not pass N+1).
- **Only the first record:** a later record longer than N does not trigger it; a first record that ends inside N does not, even when the second record is longer than N.
- **Validation:** N of zero or less raises `SqualifyException`, like `MaxBytes`; the CLI parses `--max-first-record-bytes` and rejects a non-positive or non-numeric value.
- **Failure shape (pending Q1):** the chosen outcome is pinned: the exception text, or the issue code and what scope and the profile hold (`bytesRead` is at most N+1).
- **Without a byte limit (pending Q2):** pin whichever answer is chosen: either the ceiling applies and a long first line fails, or the option is rejected without `--max-bytes`.
- **Cuts (pending Q3):** each of these is pinned to the chosen rule: a bare CR as the N-th byte (is the record N or N+1 once the LF after it is read?); a CRLF whose LF is byte N+1; UTF-16LE, UTF-16BE and UTF-32 first lines of N and N+2 or N+4 bytes (N not a multiple of the unit width); a binary file with no CR or LF (not a text record, so presumably unaffected).
- Mutation-check: changing `>` to `>=` at the boundary and dropping the early stop each fail a test above.
